title: Derived exchange
statement:
Fix the discrete commutative coefficient ring $\Lambda$ of [sk-def-pbc-conventions] and the module derived categories of [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. In the derived formulas below, $\Ex_\square$ and $\theta_\square$ are the module exchange mate and termwise square comparison of [def-kun-unbounded-exchange], restricted to the full bounded below subcategories. Inverse image is exact by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]; derived direct image restricts to $D^+$ and is computed there by bounded below injective complexes by the module-sheaf clause of [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. Hence this restriction has the displayed endpoints in $D^+$ and the same adjunction unit and counit.

At the sheaf level, the inverse-image adjunction on sheaves of sets is [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-exact]; the abelian underived exchange is [def-weil-pbc-underived-exchange]. On constant-ring module sheaves the underived exchange is the same adjoint-mate formula using [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]; its linearity and naturality are [lem-weil-pbc-underived-exchange-module-linear]. The module composition isomorphisms are [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition-module-linear]. On sheaves of sets, for $u:Y\to X$ and $v:Z\to Y$ the composition isomorphism $c_{u,v}:v^{-1}u^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}(uv)^{-1}$ is the unique isomorphism whose conjugate [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate], for $(uv)^{-1}\dashv(uv)_*$ and the composite adjunction $v^{-1}u^{-1}\dashv u_*v_*$ [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] of the set adjunctions of [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-exact], is the identification $(uv)_*F\cong u_*v_*F$ given by restriction along the canonical isomorphisms $(W\times_XY)\times_YZ\cong W\times_XZ$ [def-pc-fibre-product]; the set-level $\theta_\square$ is formed from these by the same formula as below. All occurrences of the resolution formula below concern this fixed module mate and are the bounded below case of [lem-weil-pbc-derived-exchange-module-termwise]; this is a comparison theorem, not a new definition of the exchange.

For the comment about a merely commutative square, form $\theta^0=(c_{f,g'})^{-1}c_{g,f'}$ using $fg'=gf'$ and the module composition isomorphisms just cited. For a complex $P$, naturality gives $d\,\theta^0_{P^r}=\theta^0_{P^{r+1}}\,d$ in every degree $r$, so the components form an isomorphism of complexes. Each termwise inverse-image functor preserves quasi-isomorphisms by exactness. The localization property used in [def-kun-unbounded-exchange] therefore descends this isomorphism and its inverse to the derived categories. Apply [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] to this descended square isomorphism and the edge adjunctions already specified. This construction uses only $fg'=gf'$, with no pullback identification.

Consider a cartesian square

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
X' & \xrightarrow{g'} & X\\
{\scriptstyle f'}\downarrow & & \downarrow{\scriptstyle f}\\
Y' & \xrightarrow{g} & Y.
\end{array}
$$

The commutativity of the square supplies the canonical composition
isomorphism of functors $\Sh(Y_{\Et})\to\Sh(X'_{\Et})$

$$
\theta_\square:f'^{-1}g^{-1}\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }g'^{-1}f^{-1}.
$$

Since inverse images are exact, $\theta_\square$ also denotes the induced
isomorphism of functors $D^+(Y_{\Et},\Lambda)\to D^+(X'_{\Et},\Lambda)$. (For
$F\in\Sh(X_{\Et})$ the *underived exchange map*
$\Ex^0_{\square,F}:g^{-1}f_*F\to f'_*g'^{-1}F$ in $\Sh(Y'_{\Et})$ is the
adjoint, under $f'^{-1}\dashv f'_*$, of
$f'^{-1}g^{-1}f_*F\xrightarrow{\theta_\square}g'^{-1}f^{-1}f_*F
\xrightarrow{g'^{-1}\varepsilon_f}g'^{-1}F$, with $\varepsilon_f$ the counit;
it is natural in $F$, and likewise for sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules.)

**Definition (derived exchange).** For $K\in D^+(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$, the
*exchange morphism*

$$
\Ex_{\square,K}:g^{-1}Rf_*K\longrightarrow Rf'_*g'^{-1}K
\qquad\text{in }D^+(Y'_{\Et},\Lambda)
$$

is the adjoint, under $f'^{-1}\dashv Rf'_*$, of

$$
f'^{-1}g^{-1}Rf_*K\xrightarrow{\ \theta_\square\ }g'^{-1}f^{-1}Rf_*K
\xrightarrow{\ g'^{-1}\varepsilon_f\ }g'^{-1}K
\qquad\text{in }D^+(X'_{\Et},\Lambda),
$$

where $\varepsilon_f:f^{-1}Rf_*\to\mathrm{id}$ now denotes the derived counit
on $D^+(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$. The morphism is natural in $K$, so
$\Ex_\square:g^{-1}Rf_*\to Rf'_*g'^{-1}$ is a natural transformation of
functors $D^+(X_{\Et},\Lambda)\to D^+(Y'_{\Et},\Lambda)$.

The derived adjunction exists because inverse image is exact and its right
adjoint preserves injectives. The construction needs only a commutative
square; the cartesian hypothesis matters for the question whether it is an
isomorphism. Concretely, for a bounded below injective resolution
$K\to I^\bullet$ and an injective replacement $g'^{-1}I^\bullet\to J^\bullet$,
the exchange is represented by the morphism of complexes
$g^{-1}f_*I^\bullet\xrightarrow{\Ex^0_{\square,I^\bullet}}f'_*g'^{-1}I^\bullet
\to f'_*J^\bullet$, independently of the choices.

Theta is c_{f,g'}^{-1} c_{g,f'} with the right orientation, the transpose is g'^{-1}eps_f o theta, and the commutative-square descent is sound. This matches Lean Etale.baseChange (MorphismDefs l.95-213): unit, then theta = (upperStarPlusComp f' g).symm >> eqToIso >> upperStarPlusComp g' f, then counit, with the D+ adjunction restricted from the unbounded one and only a CommSq needed. It is true because f'_* preserves K-injectives, the derived counit is the localized termwise counit and the triangle identities apply.
